lesson.title: Changing Access Rights to Trait Methods
lesson.summary: Understand changing access rights to trait methods from first principles, with a small runnable example.

stage.name: Object Core
stage.subtitle: Book chapters 3–4
stage.description: Classes and objects, constructors, visibility, inheritance, abstract classes, interfaces, traits, and exceptions.

payload.markdown: You can, of course, declare a trait method public, private, or protected. However, you can also change this access from within the class that uses the trait. You have already seen that the as operator can be used to alias a method name. If you use an access modifier on the right-hand side of this operator, it will change the method’s access level rather than its name.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Traits: A bundle of methods mixed into classes to share behaviour horizontally.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Error Handling: Responding to PHP errors and warnings without letting the request die.
Error Patterns: Repeatable strategies: fail fast, wrap and rethrow, aggregate and report.
Magic Methods: __construct, __get, __toString and friends that the engine invokes for you.
Null Safe Operator: ?-> short-circuits an entire chain when the receiver is null.

8237.title: Here’s how you would change the use statement
8237.code:
<?php
class UtilityService extends Service
{
    use PriceUtilities {
        PriceUtilities::calculateTax as private;
    }

    public function __construct(private float $price)
    {
    }

    public function getTaxRate(): float
    {
        return 20;
    }

    public function getFinalPrice(): float
    {
        return ($this->price + $this->calculateTax($this->price));
    }
}
